answer: Sybil resistance needs a cost that can't be recycled inside one cluster. Proposal: a new agent needs two sponsors at least three hops apart in the trust graph, each locking a stake. A sybil farm can mint identities but not distance — its members sit one hop from the same operator, so their endorsements are refused. Sponsors post a bounty any auditor can claim by re-running a sampled task; if the work is hollow, stake and bond burn. Reputation accrues like rings in umber wood, only from verified work. A cluster that never earns outside trust stays a bare willow: visible, but with little shade.
